data.name: Vivek
data.gender_notes: Vivek is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Vivek is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Vijñāna’ which means ‘knowledge’. The name signifies the ability to discern truth from falsehood. The sage Vivekananda, a renowned Hindu monk and philosopher, was known for his wisdom and ability to distinguish between reality and illusion. The name Vivek carries the meaning “Discrimination of the Truth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vivek usually hope their child will grow to embody discrimination of the truth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Vivek belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Discrimination of the Truth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vivek total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vivek holds great cultural significance for Hindus, as it reflects the importance placed on knowledge and wisdom. This name is often bestowed upon children to encourage them to strive for understanding and truth in their lives.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Vivek embodies the quest for knowledge and self-realization, echoing the ancient Hindu belief in the pursuit of enlightenment through the acquisition of knowledge and inner wisdom. The name is a constant reminder to seek the truth of the self and the universe, using discernment and understanding as guiding principles on one’s spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vivek signifies 'discrimination of the true from the false'. It represents the inner voice of wisdom that guides one towards the path of truth and self-realization.

vedic_reference.note: Vivek is the name of a god in Hindu mythology, a form of the god Rudra. It is also a common name in Hinduism.

historical_references.reference: Vivekachudamani, a philosophical treatise on Jñana Yoga, written in Sanskrit by Shankara, around 800 AD.
historical_references.context: This work is considered one of the most important works in Indian spirituality and is a commentary on the Bhagavad Gita, explaining the nature of Reality and the path to realization.

historical_references.reference: Vivekananda, a Hindu monk and philosopher who lived from 1863 to 1902. He was a chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and is considered a pioneer of the Hindu renaissance in India and the West.
historical_references.context: He played a key role in introducing Hinduism to the Western world through various lectures and addresses at the 1893 World's Parliament of Religions.
